precise_scope: Supporting fixed-domain transfinite compact selection, first-stage collapse for continuous outputs, exact dual test-measure reduction and fixed-current estimate, including trivial valuation. No new universal Bedford--Taylor range or counterexample.

source_status.exact_result: Two supporting lemmas, valid also with trivial valuation: (1) transfinite decreasing constructions on one unchanged ordinary domain, without intermediate sheafification, admit compact upper selection by a smooth psh generator; every finite continuous output is locally a decreasing uniform limit of smooth psh functions on a fixed compact-neighbourhood interior and lies in CPsh_1. Once-sheafified fixed-domain generation has continuous part CPsh_1 = C intersect Psh_1. This does not prove full Psh/CPsh equality. (2) For a fixed arbitrary target current T on an ordinary open W, annihilation of all continuous zero-Hessian functions is equivalent to membership of every signed T-Hessian test measure in the weak closure, against all finite continuous functions, of the real span of ambient Hessian test measures. The closure condition is not established for arbitrary T. These are support results, not a new Bedford-Taylor positive range. Universal P21.3 remains unresolved.
gaps: The fixed-domain selection proof does not handle ordinary sheafification between transfinite stages. A positive gluing argument on one neighbourhood fixed before the error tolerance is missing; full finite continuous Psh-to-CPsh conversion is not established.
Even membership of U,V in CPsh does not imply both signs of U-V are CPsh. No curvature-compatible approximation or other universal kernel argument is proved.
No proof that arbitrary target signed test measures satisfy the dual weak closure condition; distributional convergence against the ambient integration current alone is insufficient.

A continuous zero-Hessian witness obtained from failure of the dual condition has no proved representation as a difference of finite continuous psh functions, so would not alone be a P21.3 counterexample.

No analytic counterexample with all good, separated, strict, boundaryless, pure-dimensional, positivity, double-closedness, psh-pair, and upstairs equal-curvature hypotheses was found, in either valuation regime.
The new support lemmas have only a self-audit and reproducibility checks; no new independent-review or formal-verification claim is made.

result.report:
PASS is limited to the two supporting results, their first-stage corollary, and the fixed-current estimate. They hold at the manuscript’s stated scope, including trivial valuation. They do not solve universal P21.3.

I independently checked the proofs against the primary CLD v2 definitions and theorem bodies: §§8.1.1–8, 6.2.4–6 and Appendix A.2, Proposition 6.5.2, §§7.2.1/8/11–12, §§7.7.3/5, and the analytic setup in §§11.1, 13.2–3, 14.3, 15.2 and 15.7. The indispensable external inputs are listed below. Proposition 8.1.11’s disputed higher-stage identification is unnecessary. I also checked [GJR v3 §§2.2 and 5](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.05741v3#S5); no GJR theorem or prior solver verdict enters these new proofs.

For Lemma 1, upper semicontinuity and continuity of F make {v_j<F} open. These sets increase and cover the compact C, so a finite subcover yields one index covering C. With finite continuous limit u, monotonicity gives v_j≥u; applying the lemma to u+ε proves uniform convergence. Discontinuous intermediate functions therefore cause no Dini defect.

The fixed-domain construction is sound. Infima of decreasing upper semicontinuous functions remain upper semicontinuous. The iteration takes place inside a set of functions, so the cardinal stabilization argument supplies ordinal ranks. At a successor stage, compact selection chooses one child v_j on exactly the original C; induction produces a generator s≥v_j≥v on all of O. At a limit ordinal, membership in an earlier class is global by definition. Neither step inserts sheafification, changes domains, or glues positive generators. The rank-zero case uses s=v. This establishes Theorem 1 with its full obstacle and global domination conclusions.

For Theorem 2, choose C before any approximation index. Selection gives 0≤s_m−u<ε_m on C, with ε_m=3^{-m}. Constant shifts preserve the smooth Hessian. On the fixed open B=Int_O(C), q_m=s_m+ε_m satisfies ε_m≤q_m−u<2ε_m and q_{m+1}<q_m because 2ε_{m+1}<ε_m. Consequently the sequence is decreasing and uniformly convergent on B. Ordinary sheaf locality yields membership on O in CPsh and both first-stage sheaves. This locality combines membership statements; it does not construct a positive partition-of-unity approximation.

Corollary 2 also follows. Restrictions send each M_α(O) into the corresponding class on a smaller open, and compatible locally generated sections glue as functions. A first-stage uniform presentation admits selected errors δ_m=4^{-m}; shifting by 2δ_m gives δ_m<r_m−u<3δ_m and a decreasing sequence since 3δ_{m+1}<δ_m. Conversely, a continuous first-stage decreasing presentation becomes uniform after restriction to a fixed compact-neighbourhood interior by the proved Dini argument. Hence C∩M_loc=CPsh_1=C∩Psh_1. This reasoning does not flatten the full sheaf hierarchy or establish decreasing-sequence stability of M_loc.

Lemma 2 handles arbitrary singular middle-positive target currents. For a target test α of degree (n−p−1,n−p−1), η=d'd''α has complementary degree (n−p,n−p) and is symmetric. Decompose η=η_1−η_2 into compact middle-positive smooth forms. Their coefficient measures μ_i are positive and finite, with masses ⟨T,η_i⟩. Their difference defines the requested signed measure. Smooth scalar density proves independence of the decomposition. Applying support-controlled density on the complement of supp η proves cancellation there, so the signed measure is supported in supp η⊆supp α, even when the decomposition supports are larger. The ambient construction uses the original calibrated integration current throughout; component lengths are never replaced by one. Finite continuous functions may be globally unbounded because integration occurs on compact supports. At p=n−1, α is a scalar test and the same argument applies.

The current convention and symmetry justify testing only symmetric forms. Thus H_W is precisely the annihilator of L_W. Theorem 3 is an elementary annihilator argument: closure membership implies annihilation by each h∈H_W. Conversely, a basic weak neighbourhood disjoint from L_W supplies finitely many continuous evaluations. Their image of L_W is a finite-dimensional linear subspace. Orthogonal separation produces h=Σc_i f_i that annihilates L_W but not the offending target measure. This proves both directions without a current-density theorem, common support assumption, total-variation bound, or sequential-closure assertion. Positivity is needed for the coefficient measures; closedness of T is not needed for this equivalence.

The fixed-current estimate follows from |ν_{T,α}|≤μ_1+μ_2 and the differential pairing identity. Its compact C and coefficient ⟨T,η_1+η_2⟩ are chosen independently of the scalar approximation index. It therefore controls every differentiated fixed-test pairing for locally uniform scalar convergence, including against singular T. It provides continuity, not vanishing for a nonzero zero-Hessian limit.

The remaining original-target gaps are accurately stated. Equal ambient Hessians put U−V in H_W, but the draft establishes neither the dual closure for arbitrary T nor an alternative multiplier identity. Individual approximations do not make ±(U−V) CPsh or provide curvature-matched approximants. A separating continuous witness need not be a psh difference, so it would not automatically be an admissible counterexample. There is no scalar ascent, graph pullback, Poincaré–Lelong application, S1 deduction, or noninjective tropical pushforward in these proofs. No broader conclusion can be imported from the earlier attempts.

Two harmless wording corrections: CLD 8.1.12 is a Proposition, not a Lemma; and restriction compatibility should be stated as M_α(O)|_N⊆M_α(N), without suggesting that every section on N extends to O. Neither correction changes a proof. This PASS is a mathematical audit of the reconstructed supporting results, not formal verification or a priority determination.

passages.statement: CLD 8.1.1/7: on affined G-tropical spaces, Psh/CPsh are minimal ordinary sheaves generated by smooth d'd''u≥0, closed under decreasing/uniform sequences respectively; Psh allows −∞.
CLD 8.1.1/7: on affined G-tropical spaces, Psh/CPsh are minimal ordinary sheaves generated by smooth d'd''u≥0, closed under decreasing/uniform sequences respectively; Psh allows −∞.
CLD 8.1.4/8: successors use local sequential decreasing/uniform limits from the preceding stage; limit ordinals use local earlier-stage membership.
Separated Berkovich spaces over complete fields have compact-neighbourhood bases and are Hausdorff; good spaces have affinoid-neighbourhood bases (CLD 11.1.7).

Over complete fields, trivial valuation allowed, separated pure-n-dimensional analytic spaces have domain-compatible canonical CLD calibrations retaining generic lengths; boundaryless opens are locally differentially separated (11.1,13.2–3,14.3,15.2,15.7).

Over complete fields, trivial valuation allowed, separated pure-n-dimensional analytic spaces have domain-compatible canonical CLD calibrations retaining generic lengths; boundaryless opens are locally differentially separated (11.1,13.2–3,14.3,15.2,15.7).
Locally differentially separated affined G-tropical spaces admit compact smooth cutoffs and support-controlled uniform smooth approximation of C_c (CLD 6.2.4–6).

Symmetric compact smooth (q,q)-forms with paracompact locally differentially separated support-neighbourhoods decompose into two compact middle-positive smooth forms; good boundaryless analytic spaces qualify (CLD 6.5.2).

On locally differentially separated tropical spaces, middle-positive currents paired with complementary middle-positive forms give positive Radon measures; locally bounded Borel multipliers give ordinary order-zero currents (CLD 7.2.1/8/11–12).
CLD differentials preserve support; d'^2=d''^2=0, d'd''=−d''d', Jd'd''=d'd''J and ⟨d'd''S,α⟩=⟨S,d'd''α⟩ (6.4.6,7.7.3/5).
